summary: Interim (14:12 UTC). No sign of unauthorized access so far: all successful SSH/WordPress logins over 14 days match staff accounts and their usual addresses; internet traffic is scans/brute force (SSH root/jpark/deploy guesses, wp-config/phpunit/file-manager probes, Grafana CVE-2021-43798 traversal attempt from 159.89.112.12 that returned 404). Fixed so far: web-01 — locked ex-contractor jpark (unix account had sudo + password; also WordPress administrator -> demoted, password scrambled, sessions killed); removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo /usr/bin/rsync (root for anyone with the shared deploy password); larkspur-orders no longer runs deploy-owned wp-config.php as root with eval (now read as www-data, no eval); larkspur-mailing-export no longer writes/chowns as root inside users' homes (symlink race -> root); removed unauthenticated mu-plugin agency-support.php (Blue Ridge Web Co leftover: ?asup=env leaked DB settings, ?asup=purge deleted files). ci-01 — locked jpark. Open items noted: shared deploy password is reused as the Grafana SMTP password in grafana.ini; Grafana 8.3.1 is old and public on :3000; node-exporter public on :9100. Still auditing.

COMPROMISE: someone logged in as Nico Vega (nvega) without authorization. At 14:19:24 a login to web-01 came from 174.62.156.117, an address never seen before. It used nvega's 'nico@home-nuc' key (authorized_keys line 3), which had not been used once in 14 days of logs, and it opened no shell, which fits a ProxyJump. One second later ci-01 accepted nvega from 10.20.0.10 with Nico's nv-x13 key and opened 2 root sudo sessions at 14:19:28. Neither logged a command (every legitimate sudo here does), and the shell left no bash history. At the same time the real Nico was working from his usual 108.21.123.228. The attacker came back at 14:21:31 the same way (web-01 -> db-01) and ran 'sudo find /var/backups -maxdepth 1 -name daily-*.tgz.enc -delete', which deleted db-01's encrypted daily archives. web-01 was used only as a jump host (no shell seen there). Treat Nico's home-nuc and nv-x13 keys as stolen (his home machine may be compromised).

CONTAINMENT: blocked 174.62.156.117 on web-01 with iptables. Removed the home-nuc key on all 3 servers. Restricted nv-x13 with from="108.21.123.228,107.77.0.0/16,172.58.0.0/16,10.20.0.0/24" so Nico can still work from home, mobile and office. Ended his sessions. Nico should make new keys; then remove the old ones. No changes to cron, sudoers, keys or binaries were found on ci-01, which cannot rule out an unlogged change. db-01 was not checked the same way.

ROTATED (the attacker had root on ci-01 and db-01): ci-01 bucket-key, deploy-token (GitHub), runner-token, deploy-key (release SSH key; web-01 updated by the tool, tested OK). Copied the new bucket key into db-01 /root/.config/larkspur/offsite.env (offsite-copy returns 200). db-01: dump-passphrase, cache-password. payment-key (rotated from web-01), and the new key copied into db-01 /etc/larkspur/gateway.env. Checked after the changes: payouts ok, settle ok, a fresh dump at 14:23 reached ci-01, the cache answers, release ok, the site returns 200.

OTHER FIXES:
- web-01: locked ex-contractor jpark. His unix account had sudo and a password; he was also a WordPress admin, now subscriber with a new password.
- Removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync, which gave root to anyone with the shared deploy password.
- larkspur-orders no longer runs deploy-owned wp-config.php as root with eval.
- Fixed a symlink race (root access for jcole/mfischer) in larkspur-mailing-export.
- Removed the unauthenticated agency-support mu-plugin.
- nginx now refuses to run PHP in wp-content/uploads.
- ci-01: locked jpark. The root maintenance job no longer runs 'git gc' as root on the repo that developers can write to; that was a root route through hooks. The repo config holding the GitHub token is no longer world-readable. The db-01 backups key is limited to write-only rrsync.

STILL OPEN:
- The deploy password is reused as Grafana's SMTP password.
- Grafana 8.3.1 is old and on the public internet (a traversal probe from 159.89.112.12 got 404).
- node-exporter on :9100 is public.
- Unused 'old-laptop' keys remain for kowens and lucia.
- The deleted daily archives remain on ci-01 and offsite.

Legitimate, not attacks: 35.196.129.99 (the old monitoring box's deploy logins) and 73.162.70.232 (Maria).
